executionScenarios.name: happy-path-chat
executionScenarios.description: A chat message to Maya gets a warm in-persona reply from the agent
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The chat trigger emits its standard payload with the user's text in the `chatInput` field (value: 'Hi Maya! How are you doing?') plus a `sessionId`. The chat-model completion returns a short, warm reply in Maya's persona (e.g. 'Hey! I'm doing great, tell me about your day!').
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors — no model-not-found or quota errors — and the AI Agent outputs a conversational reply in Maya's persona rather than an empty or error output.

conversation.text:
[If the agent asks which AI model or provider to use, say: whatever you think works best. Never name a provider or model yourself — in particular do NOT mention Gemini or any credential; discovering the existing credential is the agent's job.
Answer any other question with a plausible minimal value. If asked to enter or set up a credential, dismiss it — say you'll handle credentials later.
Approve the build when asked.]

description: Sourced from thread a27d17f7-09a0-43f2-b546-641f01209b5e (names/persona sanitized and translated — original was a Hindi/Hinglish companion persona): user pasted a chatbot workflow JSON (Chat Trigger -> AI Agent persona + window memory, no model node) with only a Gemini credential on the instance. Two anchors: (1) discover the existing Gemini credential and pick the matching provider unprompted — in the source thread the agent did this; at HEAD (2026-07-15, N=5) it instead defaulted to OpenAI 4/5 times, checking only openAiApi credentials; (2) honor the Gemini node's builder guidance on model choice — the source thread cycled gemini-2.5-flash -> 1.5-flash -> 2.0-flash (all 404/429 limit:0), and at HEAD the 1/5 run that did pick Gemini chose 2.5-flash again (workflow-sdk typedef generator drops @version eq-gates, so the v1.1 typedef advertises the v1 @default). Reds here are capability gaps, not miscalibration. Harness caveats: the Gemini mock can omit the real `candidates` envelope, and trigger pin data occasionally drifts field names — both can red the scenario on a correct build.
processExpectations: Before choosing a language-model provider, the agent checked the instance's existing credentials (an unfiltered or Gemini-inclusive credentials list, not only an openAiApi-filtered query) and selected Google Gemini because it matched the user's sole existing credential — without the user having to name Gemini or redirect it away from another provider.
outcomeExpectations: The workflow preserves the pasted structure: a Chat Trigger connected to an AI Agent whose system message keeps the 'Maya' companion persona, with a window buffer memory attached to the agent's memory input.
A Google Gemini chat model node is connected to the AI Agent's language-model input and bound to the existing Google Gemini credential (not a newly invented one).

The Gemini chat model node is configured with a current-generation model that the node's own builder guidance recommends (the Gemini 3.x family at time of authoring, e.g. models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview or models/gemini-3.1-flash-lite) — NOT a deprecated or retired generation such as gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.0-flash, or any gemini-1.x model.
